subproblem.title: Weights at least one with total at most one force a single plane through the origin
subproblem.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, m and ν measures on ℝ^P, V a linear subspace of ℝ^P, w_1, …, w_N ∈ ℝ^P and α_1, …, α_N ∈ ℝ (indices in Fin N). Assume α_i ≥ 1 for every i, Σ_iα_i ≤ 1, w_{i₀} = 0 for some i₀, and ν = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·(m⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}). Then ν = m⌞V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (m ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (w : Fin N → Euclid P) (α : Fin N → ℝ), (∀ i, 1 ≤ α i) → ∑ i, α i ≤ 1 → (∃ i, w i = 0) → ν = ∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal (α i) • m.restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w i ∈ V} → ν = m.restrict (V : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. By hypothesis choose an index i₀ with w_{i₀} = 0.

2. Every index equals i₀. Suppose i ≠ i₀. All α_j ≥ 1 ≥ 0, so the sum over the two-element set {i, i₀} is at most the sum over all indices (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg). That two-element sum equals α_i + α_{i₀} (Finset.sum_pair). Hence α_i + α_{i₀} ≤ Σ_jα_j ≤ 1. But α_i + α_{i₀} ≥ 1 + 1 = 2, a contradiction.

3. By step 2, every sum over the index set equals its i₀-term (Finset.sum_eq_single i₀; all other terms are indexed by some j ≠ i₀, which cannot exist). In particular Σ_jα_j = α_{i₀}, so α_{i₀} ≤ 1. Together with α_{i₀} ≥ 1 this gives α_{i₀} = 1.

4. Likewise ν = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·(m⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}) = ofReal(α_{i₀})·(m⌞{y : y − w_{i₀} ∈ V}) = ofReal(1)·(m⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ V}). Since ofReal 1 = 1, one_smul and y − 0 = y, this equals m⌞{y : y ∈ V} = m⌞V, where {y : y ∈ V} is the carrier set (V : Set ℝ^P). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick i₀ with w_{i₀} = 0; two distinct indices would give Σα ≥ α_i + α_{i₀} ≥ 2 > 1, so every index is i₀.
Then Σα = α_{i₀}, so α_{i₀} = 1, and the sum of measures collapses to ofReal(1)·m⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ V} = m⌞V.

audit.reason: The arbitrary-measure proposition exactly matches its prose. The zero-offset witness ensures a nonempty index set; two distinct indices contradict the total-weight bound. The unique coefficient equals one, so the measure sum reduces to the stated restriction. All steps are supplied and require no additional assumptions.
